subject: psychiatry
title: Body-Focused Repetitive Behaviors and OCD Therapeutics

steps.tx: **Trichotillomania**, or hair-pulling disorder, involves recurrent pulling out of one's own hair resulting in noticeable hair loss, despite repeated unsuccessful attempts to decrease or stop the behavior. The scalp is the most common site, followed by eyebrows and eyelashes, characteristically yielding irregular, asymmetric patches.
steps.say: Trichotillomania involves compulsive pulling of one's hair causing asymmetric bald patches, despite repeated unsuccessful efforts to stop.

left.title: Clinical Presentation
points: Broken hair shafts of varying lengths
Scalp, eyebrows, and eyelashes most common
Absence of scalp erythema or inflammation

steps.tx: Examine the patchy scalp in this photograph, where hair is missing in an irregular pattern. The broken shafts of many different lengths are characteristic of **trichotillomania**, because hairs are pulled at different times and regrow unevenly between episodes. Unlike alopecia areata, the surface is not smooth or completely bald, and that broken, uneven texture is often the first clue at the bedside examination.
steps.say: Irregular patches with broken hairs of many lengths point to hair pulling. Unlike alopecia areata, the scalp is never smooth or completely bald here.

vis.alt: Clinical photograph of scalp trichotillomania with irregular patches of incomplete hair loss and broken hairs of different lengths
vis.caption: Clinical photograph of scalp trichotillomania, showing irregular patches of incomplete hair loss with broken hairs of varying lengths. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Trichophagia and Rapunzel syndrome** occur when hair pulling is accompanied by eating the plucked hairs, leading to the formation of an undigestible trichobezoar within the stomach. Rapunzel syndrome arises when the hairball extends into the small intestine, causing intestinal obstruction and gastric perforation.
steps.say: Ingesting plucked hair forms a gastric trichobezoar. Extension into the small bowel produces Rapunzel syndrome with severe intestinal obstruction.

nodes.label: Compulsive plucking and ingestion of hair shafts
Accumulation of insoluble keratin mass in gastric lumen
Rapunzel syndrome: tail of hair mass extends past pylorus into ileum
Mechanical bowel obstruction, ulceration, and perforation

steps.tx: **Excoriation disorder**, or skin picking disorder, is characterized by recurrent picking of one's own skin resulting in noticeable cutaneous lesions, despite repeated attempts to discontinue. Patients pick at fingernails, facial blemishes, or scabs for hours daily using fingernails or tweezers, creating scarred, ulcerated areas.
steps.say: Excoriation disorder involves chronic skin picking resulting in tissue damage and scars. It functions as a maladaptive emotional regulation habit.

rows: Lip and inner buccal mucosa biting

steps.tx: **Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale**, abbreviated Y-BOCS, is a clinician-rated 10-item instrument designed to assess the severity and type of symptoms in patients with OCD. The scale separately rates time spent, interference, distress, resistance, and control over obsessions and compulsions, scoring from zero to 40.
steps.say: The Y-BOCS scores OCD severity from zero to forty across time, interference, distress, resistance, and control over obsessions and rituals.

vis.title: Y-BOCS Severity Strata
rows: Standard baseline threshold for pharmacological trials
Extensive daily rituals; marked functional disruption
Near-constant paralyzing rituals; requires inpatient care

steps.tx: **Exposure and response prevention**, abbreviated ERP, is the first-line evidence-based psychotherapy for OCD, demonstrating efficacy equivalent or superior to medication. ERP systematically exposes the patient to obsession-triggering situations, such as touching a restroom floor, while strictly preventing them from performing the neutralizing compulsive ritual.
steps.say: Exposure and response prevention exposes patients to feared triggers while blocking compulsions, allowing conditioned anxiety to naturally habituate.

nodes.label: Controlled exposure to contamination or doubt trigger
Strict prevention of washing, checking, or mental rituals
Anxiety rises initially, plateaus, and naturally habituates
Brain learns that catastrophe does not occur without rituals

steps.tx: **Fluvoxamine and high-dose SSRIs** constitute the first-line pharmacotherapy for OCD, requiring substantially higher daily doses and longer durations to achieve therapeutic response than in depression. Doses of fluoxetine up to 80 milligrams or fluvoxamine up to 300 milligrams daily are continued for 12 weeks before declaring non-response.
steps.say: Treating OCD requires higher SSRI doses than depression, such as 300 mg of fluvoxamine daily, maintained for twelve weeks before evaluating efficacy.

vis.title: OCD Pharmacotherapy Dosing
rows: Up to 300 mg daily in divided doses
Up to 250 mg daily (monitor ECG QTc)

steps.tx: **Clomipramine** is a potent tricyclic antidepressant with exceptionally robust serotonin reuptake inhibition, historically serving as the first drug demonstrated effective in OCD. While demonstrating superior efficacy to SSRIs in meta-analyses, clomipramine is reserved for second-line therapy due to severe anticholinergic effects, sedation, and fatal cardiotoxicity in overdose.
steps.say: Clomipramine is an efficacious serotonin-dominant tricyclic for OCD, reserved for second-line use due to anticholinergic and cardiac side effects.

left.title: Clomipramine Strengths
points: Gold standard efficacy in refractory OCD
Proven in severe pediatric and adult cases

right.title: Dose-Limiting Toxicities
points: Severe dry mouth, constipation, urinary hesitancy
Lethal in overdose due to ventricular arrhythmias

steps.tx: **PANDAS syndrome**, standing for Pediatric Autoimmune Neuropsychiatric Disorders Associated with Streptococcal Infections, describes the abrupt, explosive onset of OCD or tics following Group A streptococcal pharyngitis. It is mediated by autoimmune antineuronal antibodies cross-reacting with basal ganglia antigens through molecular mimicry, managed with antibiotics and immunomodulation.
steps.say: PANDAS involves explosive overnight onset of OCD or tics after strep pharyngitis, driven by autoimmune cross-reaction against basal ganglia tissue.

nodes.label: Group A beta-haemolytic streptococcal throat infection
Molecular mimicry: antibodies cross-react with basal ganglia neurons
Overnight explosive onset of choreiform tics and severe OCD
